docRequirement: env-vars.md:78 — "Add variables under the `env` key in a `settings.json` file, creating the file if it doesn't exist. Claude Code reads them directly from the file, so they take effect no matter how `claude` was launched. A running session applies new and changed values to its environment when you save the file … Removing a variable from the file doesn't unset it in a running session". The `env` key must be readable from all four files at :91-96 (`~/.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, managed settings); :104 — each `env` entry is written into the process environment at startup and again when the file changes, "replacing the value inherited from the shell"; :106 — an empty-string value "treats the empty value as unset for provider selection" while subprocesses still inherit the empty value; :108 — a managed `env` entry overrides the same variable in user or project settings; :112 — values are reapplied to a running session on file change.
current: The `env` settings block exists on the MANAGED tier only, and there it is complete: declared at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:359 (`readonly env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>`), parsed by `parseManagedEnvBlockV1` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:932, wired at :1393-1395), written into the real process environment by `applyManagedEnv` (packages/shared/src/config/managed-env.ts:330; target defaults to `process.env` at :339, write at :352, managed-origin registry at :300-303), and re-applied on every later policy state change by `startManagedDeliveryEnvApplication` (packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts:899 → `applyManagedDeliveryEnv` :882) — started at apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1139 and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:167. USER scope has no such key: `StoredConfig` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:51-150) declares none, `StoredConfigKnownFields` (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:142-202) lists none, and `StoredConfigTopLevelSchema` is `.strict()` (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:208), so a `~/.nessy-agent/config.json` carrying `env` makes `loadStoredConfig()` throw `UnsupportedStorageLayoutError` — "config.json has an unknown or invalid top-level setting. Refusing to load it" (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:856-862). `ConfigDefaultsSchema` (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:105-141) has no `env` either. PROJECT scope is a recorded refusal, not a gap: 'env' and 'environment' are in `FORBIDDEN_SECTIONS` (packages/shared/src/plugins/project-config.ts:138) and 'env' is also in `FORBIDDEN_DEFAULTS_KEYS` (:143), diagnosed at severity error and never applied. LOCAL scope has no Nessy file at all — the project file is `.nessy-agent/config.toml` (packages/shared/src/plugins/project-config.ts:12) and there is no `.local` variant. The three Claude settings files ARE read, but only for permissions: packages/shared/src/agent/permissions-config.ts:422 routes them to `claudeSettingsPermissionDsl` (:511), which reads `root.permissions` (:518) and nothing else; the writer packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts:119 `addClaudePermissionRules` merges only the `permissions` object (:143-155), and its own test pins that an `env` block is preserved-but-never-read (packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/claude-settings-store.test.ts:81,91). No other route exists: `grep -a` for `dotenv`/`loadEnvFile` across packages/ and apps/ returns nothing, and apps/cli/src has no `--env` flag. Two partial substitutes: apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts:28 `loadShellEnv()` imports the login-shell environment into `process.env` (:74) at module load (apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:4) but is darwin-only (:30), skipped in dev (:35), and can neither add a variable the profile lacks nor override one; and the network variables the page singles out are typed user config instead (`NetworkProxySettings`, packages/shared/src/config/types.ts:27, read user-only by recorded decision at :19-25) projected per-spawn by `buildNetworkEnvVars` (packages/shared/src/config/proxy-env.ts:27, `getProxyEnvVars` :116). Subprocesses do spread `process.env` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1465, packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:240, packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/plugin-runtime-dependencies.ts:317), so the managed mechanism's `process.env` write is the working half of the contract.
divergence: Only the managed quarter of :91-96 is implemented. The delta is user scope, and it is worse than absent: the documented key name `env` is REJECTED by our user settings file — `StoredConfigTopLevelSchema` is strict (validators.ts:208) and `loadStoredConfig` fails the whole file closed (storage.ts:856), so writing exactly what the page shows breaks config loading instead of setting variables. Nothing reads an `env` block from the Claude settings files either (permissions-config.ts:518 reads `permissions` only), so the page's own example file is a silent no-op. Consequently the three semantic rules at :104/:106/:112 are unimplemented for user scope: no startup write of a settings value over the shell-inherited value (shell-env.ts:74 runs the OPPOSITE direction and nothing overrides it afterwards), no re-apply on file change (the managed tier has one, managed-delivery.ts:899; user scope has no equivalent), and no empty-string-as-unset reading. Project scope's absence is a recorded security decision (project-config.ts:138), and local scope has no file to carry the key, so neither is part of the gap — but the local-scope decision has never been recorded either way. Values, key spelling and semantics of the managed block are correct; this is a missing scope plus a strict-schema rejection, not a wrong key name.

change.what: Add `env: z.unknown().optional(),` to `StoredConfigKnownFields` (beside `networkProxy` at :198) so the strict production envelope at :208 stops refusing a config.json that carries the documented key — this one line is what turns today's startup brick into a load. Add the strict shape to `StoredConfigSchema` (:210) for validateConfig()'s report path: `env: z.record(z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/), z.string()).optional()`. Deep parsing stays in the new module, matching the comment convention already used for `sandbox`/`worktree`/`workflow`/`sessionMirror`.

Add `env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;` to `StoredConfig` (beside `networkProxy` at :143) with a comment citing env-vars.md:78 and :104. Add `getUserEnvBlock(): Readonly<Record<string,string>> | undefined` next to `getNetworkProxySettings()`, reading through `loadStoredConfig()` and the new parser. No change needed in `saveConfig` (:871) — it spreads `...config`, so the key survives a save round-trip once the envelope accepts it.

New module, sibling of managed-env.ts. (1) `parseUserEnvBlockV1(value)` with the same rules as `parseManagedEnvBlockV1` (managed-policy.ts:932): name must match `ENV_VAR_NAME`, ≤128 entries, value ≤4096 chars, reject any value containing U+0000, entry-level tolerance (one bad entry stripped, rest applies), and NO diagnostic may contain a value — a user env value is as likely to be a token as a managed one. (2) `applyUserEnv(env, { target?: Record<string, string|undefined> })` writing into `process.env` by default, which is what makes :104's 'replacing the value inherited from the shell' true (it runs after shell-env.ts's import); it MUST skip any name where `isManagedOriginEnvVar(name)` is true (managed-env.ts:303) so :108's managed-wins holds, and it must never delete a name — :78's 'Removing a variable from the file doesn't unset it in a running session' means set/replace only. Treat `""` as set-but-empty per :106 (subprocesses inherit the empty value); if provider selection is to read it as unset, that belongs at the provider-selection site, not here. (3) `startUserEnvApplication(): () => void` — apply once, then re-apply on `config.json` change (debounced `fs.watch(CONFIG_DIR)` filtered to `config.json`, the same shape as ConfigWatcher.watchGlobalConfigs at packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:410-437); do NOT hang this off `ConfigWatcherManager`, which is per-session (packages/shared/src/agent/core/config-watcher-manager.ts:211) and would apply process-wide state N times.

Call `startUserEnvApplication()` immediately after `startManagedDeliveryEnvApplication()` at :1139. Order is load-bearing and already correct: `loadShellEnv()` runs at module load (:4), so the settings block applies over the imported shell values; the managed application must stay FIRST so the managed-origin registry is populated before the user block consults it.

Same call beside `startManagedDeliveryEnvApplication()` at :167, keeping the returned stop function in the same teardown paths as `stopEnv` (:181 and the later gate branches). This is the only surface where the gap is unmitigated today — nessy-server has no shell-env import.

Decide and encode where a user `env` block sits in the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS ladder. Today the ladder is managed-env > user `tlsCaPath` > operator shell env > bundled resource, and it distinguishes managed from ambient via `managedEnvOrigin`. A user `env` entry written into process.env would enter as an indistinguishable 'operator shell' value and could silently outrank `tlsCaPath`. Either register a second origin set for user-env names and give it a defined rung, or exclude the transport/routing/credential names (`MANAGED_ENV_WITHHELD_CATEGORIES`, managed-env.ts:75) from the user block entirely and record that refusal.

Record the local-scope decision, which no file currently states: either add a Nessy local-scope settings file that may carry `env`, or refuse it the way project scope is refused (project-config.ts:138). The network-trust reasoning at config/types.ts:19-25 — nothing a `git clone` can carry may redirect the process's TLS/proxy path — argues for refusal, and a refusal is a deviation that needs a register category string so `scripts/regenerate-deviation-register.py` picks it up.

One positive and one negative for the parser (valid block applies; bad name / non-string / >4096 / NUL value stripped with a value-free diagnostic). One managed-precedence test: a name already in the managed-origin registry is not overwritten. And the mandatory disk round-trip through the PRODUCTION loader in a subprocess — copy the harness in packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/session-mirror-settings.test.ts:39-... , which exists exactly for this regression class (a key the type declares but the strict envelope never learned bricks startup).

blastRadius: Crosses a persistence boundary and a trust boundary, both risk triggers here. (1) Persistence: `env` becomes part of the on-disk config.json schema. An older build reading a config.json that carries it throws `UnsupportedStorageLayoutError` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:856) — a downgrade brick in the same class as the 8188c067 regression the session-mirror test guards. (2) Process-wide effect: the write lands in `process.env`, which every later child inherits — Pi (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1465), the Claude SDK subprocess (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:240), supervised plugin processes (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/plugin-runtime-dependencies.ts:317), and stdio MCP servers through `getProxyEnvVars` (packages/shared/src/config/proxy-env.ts:116). A user block can therefore move PATH, HTTP(S)_PROXY, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and provider-selection variables for every backend, which is why the managed tier classifies exactly those four categories (packages/shared/src/config/managed-env.ts:63-80) and why the proxy-env ladder (:82-97) has to be revisited in the same change. (3) Readers/tests to update or re-verify: packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/managed-env.test.ts (shares the origin registry and the `startManagedDelivery…` harness at :218/:244), packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/proxy-env.test.ts (the CA ladder), packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/network-trust-scope.test.ts (pins network settings as user-config-only — a user `env` route to proxy/CA variables is exactly what it exists to police), packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/session-mirror-settings.test.ts (envelope round-trip pattern), packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/claude-settings-store.test.ts:81 (asserts an `env` block is preserved and unread — still true unless the Claude-file read side is extended). (4) No RPC/wire change as scoped; surfacing the block in Settings would add one (the electron IPC `update_user_preferences` allowlist is not the writer for this key). (5) `validateConfig()` output feeds the config doctor surface, so a new strict shape changes what doctor reports.
userImpact: Concrete and worse than a no-op on the app's own settings file. A user who follows the page and adds `"env": { "API_TIMEOUT_MS": "1200000" }` to `~/.nessy-agent/config.json` does not get the variable: `loadStoredConfig()` refuses the whole file (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:856), which throws on the Electron whenReady path (apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:415) at startup, and on a live edit the ConfigWatcher reload fails and silently keeps the last-known-good config (packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:917-922) — so every OTHER setting they change afterwards also stops taking effect, with no message anywhere in the UI. A user who instead puts the block in `~/.claude/settings.json`, the file the page actually shows, gets a silent no-op: that file is read only for its `permissions` block (packages/shared/src/agent/permissions-config.ts:518). Net effect today: the only supported way to set a variable for a Nessy session is the launching shell, so on macOS the desktop app picks up whatever the login profile exports (apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts:74) and cannot be told to override it; on Windows and Linux there is no import at all; and for the headless `nessy-server` — commonly started by a service manager — there is no per-profile way to set or override anything, which is the sharpest case (a stale `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` or a wrong proxy in the unit file has no in-product remedy).
